The human validation process involves three postdoctoral researchers and five PhD students who are native Chinese speakers as introduced in Section 3.3. Each question is verified and answered by two annotators who were not involved in the question formulation.

We benchmark a series of state-of-the-art models, including seven LLMs and eight VLMs, on the Foodie dataset using zero-shot evaluation. By comparing their performance to human accuracy, we highlight the gap between open-weights and closed-weights models and demonstrate their limitations in understanding Chinese regional food culture.
guideline: Annotators answered questions based on their knowledge without using search engines and indicated 'I don't know' for out-of-domain questions.

Annotators are asked to answer the questions based on their knowledge without using search engines, this makes the task challenging as it would be hard for one to answer questions about unfamiliar foods and regions without any other available information besides names of the food.
